speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation; this is a serious presentation. To begin our assessment, are you experiencing any severe headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; you are a 22-year-old male on haloperidol for tics, presenting with fever and altered mentation but no headache, neck stiffness, or seizures. Given your medication and altered mental status, have you noticed any new muscle rigidity, tremors, or fever spikes since starting the drug?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is diagnostic for NMS.
